checks.name: Engel's law — food share falls with income
checks.statistic: r = -0.263 over 955 households; 4 of 5 quintile comparisons fall
checks.tolerance: r < 0 and at least 4 of 5 quintile comparisons falling
checks.detail: quintile mean food shares, poorest first: 39.0 %, 16.8 %, 47.4 %, 20.2 %, 12.6 %; median household spends 23.9 % of income on food. Read the levels with care: the calibrated *budget* share only binds where a household cannot afford the week of food, so the two bottom quintiles sit on the Engel curve and everybody above them is spending what the diet costs rather than what the curve allows. The law therefore emerges here rather than being imposed, which is the stronger result — and the reason the realised shares are below the budgeted ones.
